statement: A qualified small business — gross receipts (under § 448(c)(3) rules) below $5,000,000 for the taxable year and no gross receipts for any taxable year preceding the 5-taxable-year period ending with the taxable year — may elect to apply part of its § 41 research credit against payroll taxes under § 3111(f), capped at $250,000 plus an additional $250,000 for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, with no election permitted after 5 or more preceding election years (26 U.S.C. § 41(h)). Per the Form 8974 instructions, the offset is allowed beginning with the first calendar quarter after the quarter in which the income tax return making the election is filed; the credit first reduces the employer share of social security tax up to $250,000 per quarter (the first $250,000 of the election can only offset that share), any remainder reduces the employer share of Medicare tax, and unused amounts carry forward to the next quarter.
caveat: Whether expenditures are qualified research (§ 41(d)), the credit amount itself (regular vs alternative simplified computation), controlled-group aggregation, and the § 280C election are outside this card — eligibility is always a facts determination. Amounts and mechanics change; verify the live statute and instructions.
